entries.title: Low-cost Soil Moisture Sensors for Smallholder Irrigation Scheduling
entries.summary: Field trial results from Maharashtra comparing capacitive soil moisture sensors against gravimetric measurements across three cropping seasons.
entries.content:
Over three consecutive seasons we deployed 48 capacitive soil moisture probes across smallholder plots growing cotton, soybean and pigeon pea.

Sensor readings tracked gravimetric measurements with an R² of 0.91 after a simple two-point field calibration. Farmers using sensor-based scheduling reduced irrigation water use by 22% with no yield penalty.

The complete dataset and calibration procedure will be published in the October issue.

entries.title: Sub-clinical Mastitis Prevalence in Osmanabadi Goats
entries.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 312 lactating does reveals a 27% prevalence of sub-clinical mastitis detected via California Mastitis Test.
entries.content:
Sub-clinical mastitis is a silent drain on smallholder goat productivity. We screened 312 lactating Osmanabadi does across 14 villages.

Prevalence at the animal level was 27.2%, while quarter-level prevalence reached 18.9%. Staphylococcus spp. dominated the isolates. Poor udder hygiene and hand-milking on soil floors were significant risk factors.

Recommendations include pre-milking teat dipping and regular CMT screening at the village level.

entries.title: Integrated Management of Mango Hopper in Konkan Orchards
entries.summary: Combining canopy pruning, neem-based sprays and timed insecticide applications reduced hopper populations by 68% compared to farmer practice.
entries.content:
Mango hoppers (Idioscopus spp.) remain the most damaging pest during flowering in the Konkan belt.

Our IPM module—light canopy pruning after harvest, two neem oil sprays at panicle emergence and a single need-based application of a systemic insecticide—reduced hopper counts by 68% and increased fruit set by 31% relative to the calendar spray schedule most growers follow.

Input costs fell by roughly ₹4,200 per hectare.

entries.title: Biofloc Tilapia Culture in Inland Saline Water
entries.summary: Trials in Haryana demonstrate viable tilapia growth in inland saline groundwater using low-exchange biofloc systems.
entries.content:
Inland saline groundwater is a growing problem in north-western India, but it can be turned into an aquaculture asset.

We stocked GIFT tilapia at 100 fish/m³ in 10 m³ biofloc tanks using water at 8–12 ppt salinity. Over 150 days the fish reached an average of 410 g with an FCR of 1.42. Water exchange was under 5% per week.

Economic analysis suggests a payback period of about 18 months for a four-tank unit.

entries.title: Strengthening the Finger Millet Value Chain in Karnataka
entries.summary: Farmer Producer Organisations that added primary processing captured 35% higher farm-gate prices for finger millet.
entries.content:
Finger millet (ragi) has seen renewed consumer interest, but farm-gate prices lag behind retail growth.

We compared 12 FPOs in Tumakuru and Chikkaballapur districts. Those that invested in cleaning, grading and dehulling equipment captured an average of 35% higher prices, and members reported more stable demand from urban buyers.

Access to working capital remains the main constraint.

entries.title: Drone-based Pesticide Application in Paddy: Drift and Efficacy
entries.summary: Drone spraying achieved comparable pest control to knapsack sprayers while using 90% less water and 40% less labour time.
entries.content:
Agricultural drones are rapidly gaining regulatory approval in India. We evaluated a 10-litre hexacopter across 24 paddy plots in Andhra Pradesh.

Droplet deposition on the canopy was adequate at a flight height of 2 m and speed of 4 m/s. Off-target drift was measurable up to 6 m downwind under moderate breeze, highlighting the importance of buffer zones.

Efficacy against brown plant hopper matched knapsack spraying.

entries.title: Vermicompost Quality from Mixed Crop Residues
entries.summary: Mixing sugarcane trash with legume residues produced vermicompost with a C:N ratio of 14, ideal for vegetable nurseries.
entries.content:
Crop residue burning remains a persistent issue. Vermicomposting offers a productive alternative.

We tested five residue mixtures with Eisenia fetida over 75 days. A 60:40 blend of sugarcane trash and pigeon pea haulm gave the best combination of nutrient content and maturity, reaching a C:N ratio of 14 with 1.8% total nitrogen.

Nursery trials with tomato seedlings showed 23% greater seedling vigour.

entries.title: Heat Stress Mitigation in Crossbred Dairy Cattle
entries.summary: Simple shed modifications and evening feeding schedules restored 11% of milk yield lost during peak summer.
entries.content:
Temperature-humidity index values above 78 are now common for extended periods across central India.

On 36 farms we introduced roof insulation using agri-net, fogging during afternoon hours and a shift of 60% of the concentrate feed to evening hours. Milk yield recovered by 11% relative to control farms, and conception rates improved in the following season.

The interventions cost under ₹15,000 per shed.
